Subject: VM evidence request: scan retention policy, live detection telemetry, and CVE closure ledger

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looked solid. As part of our SIG/SOC2 evidence collection I need a compact packet describing Redwood's current vulnerability management evidence for two items in particular:

1) Scan retention & raw findings: We need confirmation of how long raw scan outputs and authenticated scan artifacts are retained (CSV/JSON exports), and whether you have a short-term (hot) vs archive retention split. Our policy generally requires 180 days of hot retention and 365 days archived.

2) Live detection telemetry & alert history: do you retain live/streamed detection telemetry (scan deltas, agent telemetry, first-seen timestamps) and for how long? We need timeline samples for suspicious findings (first seen -> triage -> fix).

3) CVE closure ledger: a machine-readable export showing CVE id, discovery timestamp, owner, remediation start, remediation completed, verification timestamp. We need a 90-day sample plus SLA commitments for severity buckets (critical/high/medium).

Can you provide the artifacts and a short attestation (one page) describing the cadence of scans (authenticated/full/agent), expected SLA for critical CVEs, and retention windows? Auditor will need these by end of week (Fri 18 Sep).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — include any attachments or links to the exports and an internal contact for follow-up.

Best,
Lauren Price
Security Operations Manager
FinSecure Inc.

---

Hi all — following up with the technical details and the canonical ledger mapping. Attaching the machine-readable sample via link (also included in the SharePoint packet).

Quoted summary for auditor frictionless consumption:
- Scan types & cadence:
  • Daily lightweight surface scan (unauthenticated) — focuses on open ports and known signatures.
  • Weekly authenticated full scan (credentialed) — covers internal services, container images, and host agents.
  • Monthly dependency & SCA scans — third-party libs and container image layers.

- Retention windows:
  • Findings (hot index): 180 days (searchable CSV/JSON via export).
  • Raw authenticated scan artifacts (full reports, pcap/agent logs if applicable): archived 365 days (read-only retrieval via SR ticket).
  • Incident timeline records (first-seen, triage notes, owner assignments, remediation timestamps): 540 days.
  • Aggregated telemetry for dashboards (metrics, anomaly scores): 90 days at full fidelity, 540 days aggregated.

- CVE closure SLA (default):
  • Critical (CVSS >= 9.0): remediation start <= 24 hours, fix deployed or mitigated <= 7 calendar days, verification <= 14 days.
  • High (7.0–8.9): remediation start <= 72 hours, fix <= 30 days, verification <= 45 days.
  • Medium (4.0–6.9): remediate per prioritization; target <= 90 days.

- Evidence provided:
  • vm_scan_index_20260914.csv — sample export (90-day sliding window).
  • cve_closure_log_20260915-draft.pdf — human-readable ledger and mapping to canonical CSV columns.
  • retention_policy_v2.docx — excerpt describing archival and retrieval procedure.

Attestation statement (copyable):
"Redwood Inference attests that vulnerability scanning is performed per described cadence and that raw findings are retained in hot index for 180 days with full authenticated artifacts archived for 365 days. CVE closure timelines follow the stated SLAs; exceptions are tracked and compensated by temporary mitigations and documented in the incident record."
